sections.label: Periodic Structural Inspection regime
sections.summary: BCA requires Periodic Structural Inspection every 10 years for residential and five years for non-residential buildings, with penalties for unauthorised works and PE failures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) imposes the Periodic Structural Inspection (PSI) regime to ensure that buildings are structurally safe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The PSI has to be carried out every 10 years for residential buildings and every five years for non-residential buildings, including those for industrial use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: During the inspections, the PEs must also check for any A&A works to the structure of the building and report their findings to BCA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Any A&A works not in the original BCA-approved plans would be considered unauthorised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under the Building Control Act, offenders may be liable to a fine of $200,000 or a jail term of up to two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: A PE who fails to perform his duties in carrying out the PSI according to the requirements may be liable to a fine of up to $20,000.
